text: Barsebäck Resort is a golf club located in Barsebäck, the northern part of Metropolitan Malmö in Scania, Sweden. It is one of Sweden’s premier golf facilities and has hosted the 2003 Solheim Cup as well as the Scandinavian Masters ten times between 1992 and 2017. Situated overlooking the Öresund strait, the club was established in 1969 on the grounds of Barsebäck Castle by count Ian Hamilton and his wife Marianne. It was acquired in 1974 by Gösta Carlsson, who developed it into one of Sweden’s top golfing facilities. The resort features two 18-hole courses: the 73-par Ocean Course (formerly Masters Course), completed in 1969 and designed by Ture Bruce, and the 71-par Pine Course (formerly Donald Steel Course), completed in 1989 and designed by Donald Steel, along with a 9-hole Litorina course. In 2007, Annika Sörenstam hosted a Ladies European Tour event, the Scandinavian TPC hosted by Annika, played on the Masters Course from August 9–12. The club first hosted the Scandinavian Masters in 1992, and at its tenth edition in 2017, up to 86,100 visitors attended, with 20-year-old Renato Paratore winning the tournament. Notable golfers associated with the club include Louise Stahle, Caroline Hedwall, and Henrik Stenson; the bag Stenson used to win both the FedEx Cup Playoffs and the Race to Dubai in 2013 is on display in a glass case at the clubhouse. In 2019, a 28-year-old greenkeeper died after driving his lawn mower into a water hazard. Gösta Carlsson passed away in 2018 at the age of 99. In 2020, his descendants sold the facility to Ernst Rosén, owner and operator of Vallda Golf & Country Club. The resort, renovated in 2022, includes a 36-room hotel, 28 houses for golfers, and a restaurant led by a Michelin Guide–awarded chef, Karim Khouani.
